title: Define locale-aware number input visual layer and caret behavior to avoid jumpiness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: number inputs across Redwood products (billing, quotas, runtime config) display locale formatting (group separators, decimal marks) but editing them often causes the text caret to jump or the numeric value to reflow unexpectedly. This is most visible when we apply a visual formatting layer (e.g., inserting thousands separators) on every keystroke, when users paste values, or when directionality is RTL. Browser inconsistencies (Chrome vs Safari vs Firefox, desktop vs iOS keyboard) make the behavior unpredictable.

Goals:
- Produce a UX pattern for number inputs that: 1) prevents caret-jump / reflow on user typing and paste, 2) preserves locale formatting for readability, 3) maintains keyboard accessibility and predictable selection behavior, and 4) is implementable with current runtime constraints (minimal JS overhead).

Scope: text/number input primitive used across Redwood Console (fields for quotas, pricing, timeouts), SDK config forms, and the admin billing pages. Outcome will include design spec, token recommendations for spacing/monospace fallbacks, and an engineering checklist for cross-browser QA and a11y validation.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec documents a stable editing strategy: either 'raw-edit with post-format on blur' or 'visual-format overlay with inert input' and when to choose each
Caret position is preserved during typing and paste for the chosen pattern in Chrome, Firefox, Safari (desktop) and iOS/Android browsers in the QA matrix
RTL and LTR parity: separators and caret movement behave logically under both directions
Screen reader behavior: aria-valuenow and announcements follow WCAG expectations when value changes via paste or programmatic formatting
Token additions: spacing and font-family tokens recommended (e.g., input-number-mono-font, input-number-group-token) and documented in the token proposal
Implementation checklist provided for Eng: required polyfills, event hooks (input/keydown/compositionend), tests, and known fallbacks for legacy browsers
updates: 2025-11-04 — Created ticket after multiple Console issues where numeric fields jumped caret during paste. Collected initial bug reports from Billing and Console teams.

2025-11-05 — Low-fidelity explorations completed: compared three approaches (always-raw, format-on-blur, visual-overlay). Visual-overlay feels most readable but has highest implementation complexity. Added pros/cons to doc.
2025-11-06 — Accessibility sync with Maia (A11y lead): emphasized aria-valuenow usage, avoid announcing formatting changes as separate events; prefer single atomic update when possible.

2025-11-07 — Engineering spike requested: ENG-47890 to prototype visual-overlay approach using a separate rendered layer and an ARIA-hidden formatted span. Assigned to frontend infra for feasibility estimates.

2025-11-08 — Decided to default to 'raw-edit with format-on-blur' for small numeric fields (quick edits) and 'visual-overlay' for long-read contexts (billing summary) — documented decision and next tasks for component API design.
